The search tool worked for a while after my last message. Then it returned "Server tool use limit exceeded" a second time. `submit_model` also rejects any null figure. So I can only submit a peer once all four of its figures are sourced, and I have that for Honeywell and ITW only. Honeywell's market cap is still missing.

**What I have (USD millions, FY2024)**

| Company | Revenue | EBITDA | Net income | Net debt | Market cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Honeywell | 38,498 | about 9,179 (proxy) | 5,705 | 20,146 | not found |
| ITW | 15,898 | 4,666 | 3,488 | 6,915 | not found |
| Eaton | 24,878 | not found | 3,794 | not found | 166.9bn (stockanalysis.com, current) |
| Emerson (FY Sep 2024) | not found | not found | 1,968 | not found (cash 3,588) | 90.15bn (stockanalysis.com, current) |

- **Honeywell:** Revenue, EBITDA, net income and net debt are from the sources and method I gave in my earlier message.
- **ITW:**
  - Revenue is from the 10-K.
  - EBITDA is operating income of 4,264 plus D&A of 402. Operating income comes from the qz.com report, and D&A comes from stockanalysis.com.
  - Net income is 3,488 (qz.com).
  - Net debt is total debt of 7,863 (10-K 0000049826-25-000007) less cash of 948 (stockanalysis.com).
- **Eaton:** Revenue and net income are from stockanalysis.com. Operating income is 4,673. I didn't get D&A or debt and cash.
- **Emerson:** Net income and cash are from stockanalysis.com. I didn't get revenue, operating income, D&A or debt.
- **3M and Parker Hannifin:** I have nothing usable for these two.

**Fiscal year:** The data pages I saw run through mid-2026. That means FY2025 filings exist for Honeywell and the peers. Honeywell's FY2025 figures are also restated for the Solstice spin-off. I used FY2024 because it was the only year I had in full. A reviewer should decide whether to move to FY2025 or later.

To finish, I need a working search tool. I would then pull D&A, debt and cash for Eaton, the missing Emerson lines, and Honeywell's and ITW's market caps. I'd also look for one more peer, such as Parker Hannifin. After that I would submit all five companies in one call. If you can pull those figures from your own data source and send them over, I can build and submit the model from them.
